project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Train and validate energy-specific foundation models (general-purpose models that can be adapted to several tasks) using substantial data shared securely.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Develop methods for securely sharing energy data, then train and validate energy-specific foundation models. Cover at least one operational use, such as forecasting, grid planning, congestion or fault diagnosis.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Energy model developers need enough representative data to train useful tools. Network and asset owners need controls for confidential data and operational validation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Deliver trained models, a scalable arrangement for how data is shared and evidence from both laboratory and real-life pilots.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Improve energy forecasts, grid visibility and the ability to integrate storage, renewables and flexible demand. Shared data methods should make models easier to reuse safely.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Design data governance that can operate beyond the project. Keep research outputs findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable and participate in BRIDGE (the European network for sharing smart-grid, storage and digital energy results).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners in three different eligible countries. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: Bring together data owners, application developers and model deployers. The call names utilities, grid operators and asset owners as examples of data owners and grid operators or industry as potential deployers.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: Data owners, developers and deployers should cooperate on access, training and operational validation. Show that the consortium can access substantial relevant datasets at proposal submission.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on energy foundation models and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can provide relevant datasets or validate and deploy a model for a named grid use case. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could take part in energy foundation models without receiving a grant. As an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant), it could provide relevant datasets or validate and deploy a model for a named grid use case. It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could provide relevant datasets or validate and deploy a model for a named grid use case. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources. The proposal is expected to show access to substantial relevant data.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could make suitable grid data available under controlled conditions and validate models for power flows, forecasting or fault diagnosis.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: Develop new data-sharing methods and energy models. Build on the European energy data space (a common framework for sharing sector data).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Innovation covers data governance and model development. Options include shared data connectors, training across confidential datasets and synthetic data to fill gaps.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Show access to substantial relevant datasets at submission, then develop, train and test energy models in laboratory and real-world settings.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 7–8 (technology readiness level: from a prototype demonstrated in operation to a complete, qualified system) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Perform in-depth testing in laboratory demonstrators and real-life pilots. Using a regulatory sandbox (a controlled setting for testing under supervision) is optional.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Link data owners, model developers and organisations that can use the models in operation. Design data governance that still works after funding ends.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Validate at least one energy application in depth in both laboratory and real-life pilots. Check privacy, security, transparency, explainability and whether inputs represent affected populations.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: Bring data owners, application developers and model deployers together. Grid operators can supply data, validate models or deploy them in an operational use case.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: Build privacy, security, transparency, explainability and accountability into model development. Use representative data to reduce bias and use open-source methods where feasible.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Specific conditions

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 30 million for energy foundation models. It expects 3 awards.
- Grant request: Around EUR 10 million per project. Different requests are eligible.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 169–172 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · p. 36 · Overview of this call
Data sharing to support the training and development of AI foundation models in the energy sector · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards energy foundation models.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for energy foundation models using the cost categories allowed by the grant. The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) specifies how those costs can be claimed.
- Eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow): Personnel, subcontracting and purchases are principal categories.
- Overheads and value added tax (tax on purchases): The 25% indirect-cost rate (overheads such as general office expenses) excludes subcontracting, third-party support and categories already including indirect costs.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount and Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for energy foundation models around the initial advance and later payments.
- Payment model: Pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant) usually precedes periodic payments and the final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: The mutual insurance mechanism (a common fund covering grant recovery risks) deducts 5–8% of the maximum grant from pre-financing.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for energy foundation models through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 1 December 2026, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal) with a 40-page limit.
- Opening: 4 August 2026.
cards.sources:

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for energy foundation models.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting energy foundation models is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around five months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): Around eight months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Conditions before starting: The beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) must conclude a written consortium agreement (the partners’ written agreement on how the project will run).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the portal’s forms to submit the proposal and supporting documents for energy foundation models.
- Application form: Complete online Part A and upload technical Part B and applicable annexes.
- Registration: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to funded partners) need a participant identification code before submission.
- Partner documents: The coordinator confirms its authority to act for the applicant group at submission. Participants sign declarations of honour (signed confirmations of eligibility and other requirements) before grant signature.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · Entities eligible to participate

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Energy foundation models proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation.
- Thresholds: At least 3/5 on each criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Ranking rules: Ties first favour uncovered topic aspects. The next criteria are impact then excellence.
- Weighting: The impact score (the score for what the project is expected to achieve) has a 1.5 multiplier for ranking.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · Evaluation procedure and ranking

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Show access to substantial energy datasets when applying for the energy foundation-model call.
- Conditional — Dataset access: Demonstrate at submission that you have access to large, relevant datasets.
- Optional — artificial intelligence factories: Projects may use the services of any existing artificial intelligence factory. No collaboration commitment is required.
- Conditional — Satellite data or services: Use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing where the proposal uses the covered services.
- Conditional — Consortium establishment: The destination excludes entities established in China from these Innovation Actions.
- Exception — Transfer of results: The granting authority may object to a transfer of ownership or to exclusive licensing (giving another party sole rights to use the results) for up to four years after the project ends.
